correctness.rationale: For every r-dimensional message space U, inactive coordinates are exactly the face vectors in W=U^perp. Choosing an information set P for W makes coordinate projection injective; downward closure maps each face vector in W to a face in the induced subcomplex on P. This gives the sharp upper bound on |D intersect W|, and the coordinate space F_q^P attains equality. Singleton face columns give injectivity of the message map, and r=1,k boundary cases agree with the published distance and length.

The closest primary generalized-weight paper (arXiv:2310.11873v1) formulates the subspace-intersection problem, explicitly says the general simplicial-complex maximum is difficult, and proceeds to special cases. residual_risks: A differently phrased equivalent information-set compression lemma may exist in older down-set or monomial-code literature without using generalized-Hamming-weight terminology.

The 2023/2025 paper uses a broader q-ary support-downset notion, whereas the accepted claim is deliberately scoped to the 2026 characteristic-face construction; no claim is made here about every variant called a simplicial code.

value.rationale: The theorem computes the complete higher-weight hierarchy of the arbitrary-complex family through a fixed-cardinality induced-subcomplex extremum, replaces optimization over all linear subspaces by coordinate choices, proves field independence, and subsumes the published minimum-distance formula. This is a structural reduction with direct relevance to higher-weight questions, not a routine numerical extension.
